A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SHiP ultrametric-clustering work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime, ARI and NMI evaluations, together with qualitative clustering examples (Tables 2–3 and 5–7; Figures 4–5).

after.justification: v2 retains original clustering and runtime evaluations and adds AMI and correlation-coefficient results in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The sorted center/cost-decrease construction, clustering objectives, partitioning methods, Median-of-Elbows and Euclidean tie-breaking remain unchanged. The additional farthest-first pseudocode formalizes an existing procedure; the implementation algorithms in v1 Appendix E and v2 Appendix D are substantively retained.

E1.justification: The benchmark suite is retained, but the Iris toy experiment shown in v1 Figure 5 disappears. Compound remains in the benchmark tables, Moons remains in v2 Figure 2, and the D31 visualization moves to Figure 8.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark tables retain Euclidean k-means, SCAR, Ward, AMD-DBSCAN and DPC. The retained Moons comparison also keeps HDBSCAN, Euclidean k-means and Ward; the Cover-tree, KD-tree and HST-DPO alternatives remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds AMI and correlation coefficient to the existing ARI/NMI evaluation. Its runtime description changes Euclidean k-means from k=10 to ground-truth k, agreeing with table headings already present in v1; this correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The Compound and Iris qualitative failure comparisons in v1 Figure 5 are removed, while Moons is retained. Existing ultrametric/hierarchy/partition comparisons and tie-breaking runtime analysis remain; relocating the D31 visualization does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Ten-run evaluations and uncertainty entries already appear in v1's appendix tables. v2 explicitly identifies reported values as means and the uncertainty for nondeterministic algorithms as standard deviations. This clarifies reporting without documenting an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 add full AMI and correlation-coefficient comparisons across the retained benchmarks, substantially extending the reported quantitative results. Existing runtime and NMI table entries and ARI means remain unchanged. D31's AMD-DBSCAN ARI changes from 86.4 ± 0.1 to 86.4, and the combined runtime displayed in Figure 3/3a changes from 9.076 to 9.099 seconds.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 corrects the LCA construction from d ≤ dmax to d < dmax, preserves nonzero leaf self-distances, and supplies the missing necessity proof for Corollary 3.4. Appendix A.3 replaces the informal k-center cost characterization with Fact A.2 and revises the optimality and hierarchy arguments. These are substantive proof changes despite retaining the headline theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract's optimality, hierarchical-solution and fast-reuse claims remain intact. v2 additionally claims the first comprehensive evaluation of HSTs across clustering tasks in Section 2 and makes their poor clustering quality a central conclusion in Section 8.

C2.justification: v2 develops the HST results into a broader concern about their suitability for precision-sensitive machine learning and explicitly identifies dependence on ultrametric choice as a limitation. It removes v1 Section 4.1.2's specific caveats about arbitrary elbow selection and its restricted choice of partitions.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses the experimental default μ=5 and replaces the anonymous code link with public repository and Python-package links. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit Python 3.12 and pybind11 details. Hardware information and HST implementation sources remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: A substantial Related Work section adds literature on ultrametric applications, tree clustering, hierarchical segmentation and approximation algorithms. It explicitly positions the approach as generalizing Cohen-Addad et al.'s 2021 Algorithm 2 and distinguishes its assumptions and runtime from earlier tree-clustering results, replacing v1's brief comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, practical explanations, experimental discussion and conclusion, introduces a dedicated Related Work section, and consolidates the theoretical appendices. The motivating example moves into the introduction, and proof exposition is extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure and table rearrangement. Runtime and elbow plots become Figure 3a–b, D31 panels move to the appendix, the toy comparison is reduced to Moons, and a new marking-procedure diagram and two metric tables are added.

improvement.justification: The corrected LCA construction and added converse proof, clearer research positioning, and additional AMI/correlation comparisons improve justification and assessability. Some software-environment details are lost, and v2 Lemma A.13 retains v1 Lemma B.8's erroneous inequality when dropping a subtracted nonnegative cost. The revision therefore makes useful improvements without resolving the theory's remaining proof problems.
